Jon.2.2.bsb: saying: “In my distress I called to the LORD, and He answered me. From the belly of Sheol I called for help, and You heard my voice.
Jon.2.2.kjv: And said, I cried by reason of mine affliction unto the Lord, and he heard me; out of the belly of hell cried I, and thou heardest my voice.

Jon.2.10.bsb: And the LORD commanded the fish, and it vomited Jonah onto dry land.
Jon.2.10.kjv: And the Lord spake unto the fish, and it vomited out Jonah upon the dry land.

Jon.2.1.bsb: From inside the fish, Jonah prayed to the LORD his God,
Jon.2.1.kjv: Then Jonah prayed unto the Lord his God out of the fish’s belly,

Jon.1.1.bsb: Now the word of the LORD came to Jonah son of Amittai, saying,
Jon.1.1.kjv: Now the word of the Lord came unto Jonah the son of Amittai, saying,

Jon.1.16.bsb: Then the men feared the LORD greatly, and they offered a sacrifice to the LORD and made vows to Him.
Jon.1.16.kjv: Then the men feared the Lord exceedingly, and offered a sacrifice unto the Lord, and made vows.

Jon.2.9.bsb: But I, with the voice of thanksgiving, will sacrifice to You. I will fulfill what I have vowed. Salvation is from the LORD!”
Jon.2.9.kjv: But I will sacrifice unto thee with the voice of thanksgiving; I will pay that that I have vowed. Salvation is of the Lord.

Jon.4.4.bsb: But the LORD replied, “Have you any right to be angry?”
Jon.4.4.kjv: Then said the Lord, Doest thou well to be angry?

Jon.4.1.bsb: Jonah, however, was greatly displeased, and he became angry.
Jon.4.1.kjv: But it displeased Jonah exceedingly, and he was very angry.

Jon.4.2.bsb: So he prayed to the LORD, saying, “O LORD, is this not what I said while I was still in my own country? This is why I was so quick to flee toward Tarshish. I knew that You are a gracious and compassionate God, slow to anger, abounding in loving devotion—One who relents from sending disaster.
Jon.4.2.kjv: And he prayed unto the Lord, and said, I pray thee, O Lord, was not this my saying, when I was yet in my country? Therefore I fled before unto Tarshish: for I knew that thou art a gracious God, and merciful, slow to anger, and of great kindness, and repentest thee of the evil.

Jon.4.9.bsb: Then God asked Jonah, “Have you any right to be angry about the plant?” “I do,” he replied. “I am angry enough to die!”
Jon.4.9.kjv: And God said to Jonah, Doest thou well to be angry for the gourd? And he said, I do well to be angry, even unto death.

Jon.2.4.bsb: At this, I said, ‘I have been banished from Your sight; yet I will look once more toward Your holy temple.’
Jon.2.4.kjv: Then I said, I am cast out of thy sight; yet I will look again toward thy holy temple.

Jon.1.3.bsb: Jonah, however, got up to flee to Tarshish, away from the presence of the LORD. He went down to Joppa and found a ship bound for Tarshish. So he paid the fare and went aboard to sail for Tarshish, away from the presence of the LORD.
Jon.1.3.kjv: But Jonah rose up to flee unto Tarshish from the presence of the Lord, and went down to Joppa; and he found a ship going to Tarshish: so he paid the fare thereof, and went down into it, to go with them unto Tarshish from the presence of the Lord.

Jon.2.7.bsb: As my life was fading away, I remembered the LORD. My prayer went up to You, to Your holy temple.
Jon.2.7.kjv: When my soul fainted within me I remembered the Lord: and my prayer came in unto thee, into thine holy temple.

Jon.4.8.bsb: As the sun was rising, God appointed a scorching east wind, and the sun beat down on Jonah’s head so that he grew faint and wished to die, saying, “It is better for me to die than to live.”
Jon.4.8.kjv: And it came to pass, when the sun did arise, that God prepared a vehement east wind; and the sun beat upon the head of Jonah, that he fainted, and wished in himself to die, and said, It is better for me to die than to live.

Jon.2.3.bsb: For You cast me into the deep, into the heart of the seas, and the current swirled about me; all Your breakers and waves swept over me.
Jon.2.3.kjv: For thou hadst cast me into the deep, in the midst of the seas; and the floods compassed me about: all thy billows and thy waves passed over me.

Jon.2.5.bsb: The waters engulfed me to take my life; the watery depths closed around me; the seaweed wrapped around my head.
Jon.2.5.kjv: The waters compassed me about, even to the soul: the depth closed me round about, the weeds were wrapped about my head.

Jon.2.6.bsb: To the roots of the mountains I descended; the earth beneath me barred me in forever! But You raised my life from the pit, O LORD my God!
Jon.2.6.kjv: I went down to the bottoms of the mountains; the earth with her bars was about me for ever: yet hast thou brought up my life from corruption, O Lord my God.

Jon.2.8.bsb: Those who cling to worthless idols forsake His loving devotion.
Jon.2.8.kjv: They that observe lying vanities forsake their own mercy.

Jon.3.5.bsb: And the Ninevites believed God. They proclaimed a fast and dressed in sackcloth, from the greatest of them to the least.
Jon.3.5.kjv: So the people of Nineveh believed God, and proclaimed a fast, and put on sackcloth, from the greatest of them even to the least of them.

Jon.3.10.bsb: When God saw their actions—that they had turned from their evil ways—He relented from the disaster He had threatened to bring upon them.
Jon.3.10.kjv: And God saw their works, that they turned from their evil way; and God repented of the evil, that he had said that he would do unto them; and he did it not.

Jon.1.9.bsb: “I am a Hebrew,” replied Jonah. “I worship the LORD, the God of the heavens, who made the sea and the dry land.”
Jon.1.9.kjv: And he said unto them, I am an Hebrew; and I fear the Lord, the God of heaven, which hath made the sea and the dry land.

Jon.4.10.bsb: But the LORD said, “You cared about the plant, which you neither tended nor made grow. It sprang up in a night and perished in a night.
Jon.4.10.kjv: Then said the Lord, Thou hast had pity on the gourd, for the which thou hast not laboured, neither madest it grow; which came up in a night, and perished in a night:

Jon.4.11.bsb: So should I not care about the great city of Nineveh, which has more than 120,000 people who cannot tell their right hand from their left, and many cattle as well?”
Jon.4.11.kjv: And should not I spare Nineveh, that great city, wherein are more than sixscore thousand persons that cannot discern between their right hand and their left hand; and also much cattle?

Jon.1.4.bsb: Then the LORD hurled a great wind upon the sea, and such a violent storm arose that the ship was in danger of breaking apart.
Jon.1.4.kjv: But the Lord sent out a great wind into the sea, and there was a mighty tempest in the sea, so that the ship was like to be broken.

Jon.1.17.bsb: Now the LORD had appointed a great fish to swallow Jonah, and Jonah spent three days and three nights in the belly of the fish.
Jon.1.17.kjv: Now the Lord had prepared a great fish to swallow up Jonah. And Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.

Jon.4.6.bsb: So the LORD God appointed a vine, and it grew up to provide shade over Jonah’s head to ease his discomfort, and Jonah was greatly pleased with the plant.
Jon.4.6.kjv: And the Lord God prepared a gourd, and made it to come up over Jonah, that it might be a shadow over his head, to deliver him from his grief. So Jonah was exceeding glad of the gourd.

Jon.1.5.bsb: The sailors were afraid, and each cried out to his own god. And they threw the ship’s cargo into the sea to lighten the load. But Jonah had gone down to the lowest part of the vessel, where he lay down and fell into a deep sleep.
Jon.1.5.kjv: Then the mariners were afraid, and cried every man unto his god, and cast forth the wares that were in the ship into the sea, to lighten it of them. But Jonah was gone down into the sides of the ship; and he lay, and was fast asleep.

Jon.1.14.bsb: So they cried out to the LORD: “Please, O LORD, do not let us perish on account of this man’s life! Do not charge us with innocent blood! For You, O LORD, have done as You pleased.”
Jon.1.14.kjv: Wherefore they cried unto the Lord, and said, We beseech thee, O Lord, we beseech thee, let us not perish for this man’s life, and lay not upon us innocent blood: for thou, O Lord, hast done as it pleased thee.

Jon.3.1.bsb: Then the word of the LORD came to Jonah a second time:
Jon.3.1.kjv: And the word of the Lord came unto Jonah the second time, saying,

Jon.3.2.bsb: “Get up! Go to the great city of Nineveh and proclaim to it the message that I give you.”
Jon.3.2.kjv: Arise, go unto Nineveh, that great city, and preach unto it the preaching that I bid thee.

Jon.3.9.bsb: Who knows? God may turn and relent; He may turn from His fierce anger, so that we will not perish.”
Jon.3.9.kjv: Who can tell if God will turn and repent, and turn away from his fierce anger, that we perish not?

Jon.3.8.bsb: Furthermore, let both man and beast be covered with sackcloth, and have everyone call out earnestly to God. Let each one turn from his evil ways and from the violence in his hands.
Jon.3.8.kjv: But let man and beast be covered with sackcloth, and cry mightily unto God: yea, let them turn every one from his evil way, and from the violence that is in their hands.

Jon.3.6.bsb: When word reached the king of Nineveh, he got up from his throne, took off his royal robe, covered himself with sackcloth, and sat in ashes.
Jon.3.6.kjv: For word came unto the king of Nineveh, and he arose from his throne, and he laid his robe from him, and covered him with sackcloth, and sat in ashes.

Jon.3.7.bsb: Then he issued a proclamation in Nineveh: “By the decree of the king and his nobles: Let no man or beast, herd or flock, taste anything at all. They must not eat or drink.
Jon.3.7.kjv: And he caused it to be proclaimed and published through Nineveh by the decree of the king and his nobles, saying, Let neither man nor beast, herd nor flock, taste any thing: let them not feed, nor drink water:

Jon.1.2.bsb: “Get up! Go to the great city of Nineveh and preach against it, because its wickedness has come up before Me.”
Jon.1.2.kjv: Arise, go to Nineveh, that great city, and cry against it; for their wickedness is come up before me.
